In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Fath (The Victory)

It was named thus because it indicates the opening of lands, proofs, miracles and realities; and there follow from each of these forgiveness, the completion of blessing, guidance, and mighty victory. All of these are magnificent matters, as al-Mahayimi notes.

Its verses number twenty-nine, and it is Medinan. It was revealed upon the return of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from al-Hudaybiyah in the sixth year of the Hijrah, as a promise to him of victory. Anas said: "When we returned from al-Hudaybiyah, and we had been prevented from performing our rites, we were in grief and distress, and then it was revealed."

There is disagreement about the place where it was revealed. Muhammad ibn Sa'd has (Bi-Dajnan), spelled with an unpointed dad, a sukun on the jim, and a light nun. Al-Hakim, in al-Iklil, has (Kura' al-Ghamim). And from Abu Ma'shar: (al-Juhfah).

The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: The three places are close to one another.

Al-Bukhari narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ), while on one of his journeys, said to Umar: "A surah has been revealed to me tonight which is dearer to me than all that the sun rises upon."

He also narrated from Abdullah ibn Mughaffal, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) recited Surah al-Fath on the day of the conquest of Makkah, and he trilled in it."

Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim

Discourse on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying:

[1] ﴿Indeed, We have given you a clear victory.﴾

﴿Indeed, We have given you a clear victory.﴾ Al-Razi said: There are several meanings of "victory" (al-fath):

The first: the conquest of Makkah, which is evident.

The second: the conquest of Rome and others.

The third: that by "victory" is meant the treaty of al-Hudaybiyah.

The fourth: the opening of Islam through argument and proof, and through the sword and the spear.

The fifth: that by it is meant judgement, as in His saying: ﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth﴾ [al-A'raf: 89], and His saying: ﴿Then will He judge between us in truth﴾ [Saba': 26]. End of quote.

It is not hidden that all the aforementioned meanings are such that the divine victory applies to them, and all of them have had their fulfilment realised. However, the occasion of revelation of the verse, whose time the trustworthy transmitters have preserved, explains the intended meaning of "victory" with an explanation admitting no disagreement, and that is the third meaning mentioned.

The Imam Ibn Kathir said: This noble surah was revealed when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from al-Hudaybiyah, in Dhu al-Qa'dah of the sixth year of the Hijrah, when the polytheists prevented him from reaching the Sacred Mosque to perform his umrah there, and they stood between him and that; then they inclined toward reconciliation and truce, that he should return that year and come back the following year. He accepted this, despite the dislike of a group of the Companions, among them Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with them, as its detail will come in its place in the tafsir of this surah, Allah willing. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sacrificed his offering where he had been held back and returned, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed (p-٥٣٩٦) this surah concerning what had occurred between him and them, and made that treaty a victory, in consideration of the benefit in it and of what the matter ultimately led to, as narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, and others, that he said: "You count the victory as the conquest of Makkah, but we count the victory as the treaty of al-Hudaybiyah." And from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "We did not count the victory except as the day of al-Hudaybiyah." Al-Bukhari narrated from al-Bara', may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "You count the victory as the conquest of Makkah, and indeed the conquest of Makkah was a victory, but we count the victory as the Pledge of Ridwan on the day of al-Hudaybiyah."

Imam Ahmad narrated from Anas ibn Malik who said: "There was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿That Allah may forgive you your past and future sins﴾ [al-Fath: 2], on his return from al-Hudaybiyah. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'There has been revealed to me a verse dearer to me than everything upon the earth,' and then the Prophet (ﷺ) recited it to them." Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it in the Two Sahihs from the narration of Qatadah.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Majma' ibn Jariyah al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with him, who was one of the reciters who had recited the Qur'an, who said: "We witnessed al-Hudaybiyah, and when we turned away from it, behold, the people were driving the camels hard. The people said to one another: 'What is wrong with the people?' They said: 'Revelation has come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' So we went out with the people hurrying, and behold, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was on his riding beast at Kura' al-Ghamim. The people gathered around him, and he recited to them: ﴿Indeed, We have given you a clear victory.﴾"

He said: A man from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Messenger of Allah! Is this a victory?" He (ﷺ) said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad! It is indeed a victory." Abu Dawud narrated it in the chapter on Jihad.

Then Ibn Kathir said: So what is meant by His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have given you a clear victory﴾ - that is, manifest and evident - is the treaty of al-Hudaybiyah, for by means of it there came abundant good, people were made secure, they mingled with one another, the believer spoke with the disbeliever, and beneficial knowledge and faith spread. End of quote.

(p-٥٣٩٧) And the Imam Ibn al-Qayyim said in Zad al-Ma'ad, in his discussion of what the Ghazwah of al-Hudaybiyah contains of jurisprudence and subtleties, the following, in substance: The treaty of al-Hudaybiyah was a preface and a paving the way before this great victory. People became secure by it, they spoke with one another, and debated with one another about Islam, and those among the Muslims in Makkah who had been hidden were enabled to openly manifest their religion, to call to it, and to debate concerning it, and a great multitude entered Islam by means of it. For this reason Allah called it a victory in His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have given you a clear victory﴾, revealed concerning al-Hudaybiyah, and Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah! Is this a victory?" He said: "Yes." And He, glory be to Him, repeated the mention of its being a victory, saying: "a near victory." This is His, glory be to Him, manner: to place before great matters preliminaries that serve as an entrance to them, announcing them and pointing to them, just as He placed before the story of the Messiah and his creation without a father the story of Zakariyya and the creation of a child for him despite his old age, when such a one does not beget children. And as He placed before the abrogation of the qiblah the story of the House, its building, its exaltation, the mention of its builder, his glorification and praise. And before all of that He paved the way by mentioning abrogation, its wisdom which necessitates it, and His all-encompassing power over it. Likewise what He placed before the mission of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): the story of the Elephant, the predictions of the soothsayers about him, and other things. Likewise the good true dream of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was a preface before the revelation in wakefulness. Likewise the Hijrah was a preface before the command to jihad. Whoever reflects on the secrets of the Shari'ah and of divine decree will see in that what its wisdom dazzles the people of understanding with. End of quote. And His, the Exalted's, saying:

The commentary on His saying, Exalted is He:

[2] ﴿That Allah may forgive you your past and future sins, complete His favor upon you, and guide you to a straight path﴾.

﴿That Allah may forgive you﴾. Abu al-Su'ud said: This is the purpose of the conquest (al-fath), insofar as it follows from his peace be upon him striving to raise the word of Allah Exalted, by enduring the hardships of the struggle and plunging into the sources of calamities (p-٥٣٩٨). ﴿Your past and future sins﴾, that is, all that preceded from you of leaving what was better (tark al-awla). Calling it a sin is in view of his lofty station.

Ibn Kathir said: This is one of his peculiarities, peace be upon him, in which no one else shares, and there is no authentic hadith about the reward of deeds that states, as it does for others, that his past and future sins are forgiven. In this there is a great honor for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in all his affairs, in obedience, righteousness and steadfastness, which no human other than him has attained, neither among the earlier nor the later generations. He (ﷺ) is the most perfect of humankind absolutely, and their master in this world and the Hereafter. Since he was the most obedient of Allah's creatures to Allah, and the most mindful of honoring His commands and prohibitions, when his she-camel knelt with him, he said: "The one who held back the elephant has held her back." Then he (ﷺ) said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, they will not ask me today for anything by which they honor the sanctities of Allah except that I will grant it to them." So when he obeyed Allah in that and agreed to the truce, Allah Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, We have given you a clear victory﴾ [al-Fath: 1], and the verses that follow.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And complete His favor upon you﴾, that is, by making you prevail over your enemy and raising your mention. ﴿And guide you to a straight path﴾, that is, guide you to a way of religion in which there is no crookedness. Abu al-Su'ud said: The essence of steadfastness, although it was already present before the conquest, there came about after it, through the clarification of the path of truth and the straightness of its methods, what had not been present before it.

The discourse on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[3] ﴿And God will help you with a mighty help.﴾

﴿And God will help you with a mighty help.﴾ That is: a strong and invincible help, which no conqueror can overcome and no repeller can repel, [granting] the might by which God strengthens you and the victory with which He supports you.

(p-5399)

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[4] ﴿It is He who sent down tranquility (al-sakinah) into the hearts of the believers, that they might increase in faith along with their faith. And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾

﴿It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers﴾ That is, stillness and assurance in faith and in the truth. ﴿That they might increase in faith along with their faith﴾ That is, a certainty joined to their certainty.

Al-Qashani said: Tranquility is a light in the heart by which it settles upon its witnessed object and is reassured. It is among the beginnings of ʿayn al-yaqin (the certainty of direct witnessing), after ʿilm al-yaqin (the certainty of knowledge). It is as if it were a certain perception accompanied by delight and joy.

﴿And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth﴾ That is, helpers through whom He takes vengeance on whomever He wills of His enemies. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ That is, in His decree and His management.

**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

[5] ﴿That He may admit the believing men and the believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, and remove from them their misdeeds. And that is, with Allah, a great achievement.﴾

The lām (اللَّامُ) in His saying ﴿That He may admit the believing men and the believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein﴾ is related to an omitted element, such as: "He commanded jihad so that He might admit…" etc. Or, "He arranged what He arranged of what was mentioned for that purpose." It may also be related to ﴿We have given you a clear victory﴾ (al-Fath: 1), on the basis that the first relates to it absolutely and this one with a restriction. Or it may be related to His saying ﴿that they might increase﴾ (al-Fath: 4), and ﴿and remove from them their misdeeds, and that is, with Allah, a great achievement﴾.

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[6] ﴿And He will punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and polytheist women, who assume about Allah an assumption of evil. Upon them is a circle of evil, and Allah has become angry with them and has cursed them and prepared for them Hell, and evil is it as a destination.﴾

(p-5400) ﴿And He will punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and polytheist women, who assume about Allah an assumption of evil﴾: that is, the assumption of an evil matter, namely that Allah, exalted is He, would not grant victory to His Messenger and the believers. ﴿Upon them is a circle of evil﴾: that is, punishment in this world through various calamities, such as killing, humiliation, and abasement. It is also read ﴿dā'iratu l-sū'** (*dā'iratus-sau'*) with a damma, and both are dialectal forms of (sā'a), like al-kurh and al-karh (both meaning hatred). ﴿And Allah has become angry with them﴾: that is, by subjugation and veiling. ﴿And has cursed them﴾: that is, by expulsion and removal (from mercy) in the Hereafter. ﴿And He has prepared for them Hell, and evil is it as a destination.﴾

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[7] ﴿And to Allah belongs the armies of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is ever Exalted in Might, Wise.﴾

﴿And to Allah belongs the armies of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is ever Exalted in Might, Wise.﴾ It has been said concerning the secret of the repetition: it was mentioned earlier with the meaning that He is the Manager of the affairs of creation according to the requirement of His wisdom, so He followed it with His saying: ﴿Knowing, Wise﴾ [al-Fath: 4]. Here it is intended as a threat, that they are in the grip of the power of the Avenger, so He followed it with His saying: ﴿Exalted in Might, Wise﴾, and there is no repetition. It has also been said: the armies are armies of mercy and armies of punishment, and the intended meaning here is the second, which is why He addressed the attribute of might. Al-Qashani said: He repeated it to convey the dominance of the earthly armies over the heavenly ones concerning the hypocrites and the polytheists, in contrast to what He did with the believers. And He substituted "Knowing" with "Exalted in Might" to convey the meaning of subjugation and suppression, because knowledge is of the category of gentleness, while might is of the category of subjugation.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[8] ﴿Indeed, We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾.

﴿Indeed, We have sent you as a witness﴾, i.e., over your nation, concerning what they answered you with regarding that to which you called them. ﴿And a bringer of good tidings﴾, i.e., to those who responded to you, with Paradise. ﴿And a warner﴾, i.e., to those who opposed you, with the Fire.

(p-5401)

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[9] ﴿That you may believe in Allah and His Messenger, and support him and honor him, and exalt Him morning and evening.﴾

﴿That you may believe in Allah and His Messenger, and support him﴾: i.e., you strengthen His religion, and uphold it. ﴿And honor him﴾: i.e., you magnify him. ﴿And exalt Him morning and evening﴾: i.e., at dawn and at dusk, taken literally, or continually, by making the two ends of the day a metaphor (kinayah) for the whole. This is like saying "east and west," meaning the entire world. All the pronouns, according to what we have mentioned, refer to Allah. He also permitted that the first two refer to the Messenger and the last to Allah, but in that there is a disjunction (tafkik).

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:**

[10] ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, they are only pledging allegiance to Allah. The hand of Allah is over their hands. So whoever breaks his pledge, breaks it only to his own detriment, and whoever fulfills what he has covenanted with Allah, He will give him a great reward.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you﴾, i.e., to fight the Quraysh beneath the tree, and not to flee when they meet the enemy, nor to turn their backs to them. ﴿they are only pledging allegiance to Allah﴾, i.e., because the making of the covenant with the Messenger of Allah is like making it with Allah, without any difference, since the purpose of confirming the pact is to observe His commands and prohibitions. ﴿The hand of Allah is over their hands﴾ is an emphasis on what precedes it. That is, the hand of Allah at the pledge is above their hands, as if they were pledging allegiance to Allah through their pledge to His Prophet (ﷺ). Al-Qashani said: That is, His manifest power is in the hand of the Messenger, above their manifest power in the forms of their hands, so it harms them when they break the pledge and benefits them when they fulfill it.

﴿So whoever breaks﴾, i.e., violates his pledge, ﴿breaks it only to his own detriment﴾, i.e., because the harm of that returns to him alone. ﴿And whoever fulfills what he has covenanted with Allah, He will give him a great reward﴾, which is Paradise.

**Note:**
This pledge was the Pledge of Ridwan (Bay'at al-Ridwan). It took place beneath a sumrah tree (a kind of acacia) at al-Hudaybiyah. The number of Companions who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on that day was one thousand four hundred, and it is said: three hundred, and it is said: five hundred. The first figure is the most accurate, according to what Ibn Kathir said. Many of the imams have related its account in detail. And since this entire glorious surah concerns it, it was necessary to cite it in full.

Ibn Ishaq said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) set out in Dhu al-Qa'dah intending the minor pilgrimage (umrah), not seeking war. He called upon the Arabs and those around him from the Bedouin tribes to go out with him, but he feared that the Quraysh would confront him with war or prevent him from the House. So many of the Bedouins were slow to respond. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out with those of the Muhajirun and the Ansar who were with him, and those of the Arabs who joined him. He drove the sacrificial animals (hady) with him and entered into ihram for the umrah, so that people would be safe from his war, and so that people would know that he had only come out as a visitor to this House and to honor it."

Ibn al-Qayyim said: The story of al-Hudaybiyah took place in the sixth year, in Dhu al-Qa'dah. He had with him one thousand five hundred. This is how it is in the (al-Sahihayn, the two Sahih collections) from Jabir. In both of them, from Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa: "We were one thousand three hundred." And from Jabir in both: "They were one thousand four hundred", and the heart inclines more to this, and it is the statement of al-Bara' ibn Azib, Ma'qil ibn Yasar and Salamah ibn al-Akwa'. Then, when they reached Dhu al-Hulayfah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) garlanded the sacrificial animals, marked them, entered into ihram for the umrah, and sent ahead of him a scout from Khuza'ah to inform him about the Quraysh. When he was near Usfan, his scout came to him and said: "I left Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy; they have gathered the Ahabish for you, gathered their hosts for you, and they will fight you and bar you from the House."

The Prophet (ﷺ) consulted his Companions and said: "Do you see that we should turn toward the offspring of these people who aided them, and strike them? If they remain seated, they will remain seated aggrieved and sorrowful, and if they escape, they will be a neck which Allah has cut off? Or do you see that we should head for the House, and whoever bars us from it, we fight him?" Abu Bakr said: "Allah and His Messenger know best! We have come only as those making umrah, and we did not come to fight anyone. But whoever stands between us and the House, we will fight him." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Then move on." So they moved on, until when they were in part of the way, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Khalid ibn al-Walid is at al-Ghamim with the cavalry of the Quraysh, so take the right-hand way." By Allah, Khalid did not perceive them until he saw the dust of the army. He set off galloping as a warner to the Quraysh. The Prophet (ﷺ) continued until, when he reached the mountain pass that descends to them, his she-camel knelt down. The people said: "Hal, hal!" but she persisted. They said: "Al-Qaswa' has stopped! Al-Qaswa' has stopped!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Al-Qaswa' has not stopped, nor is that her habit, but the one who stopped her is the One who stopped the elephant!" Then he said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, they will not ask me for any arrangement in which they honor the sacred things of Allah, except that I will give it to them."

Then he urged her on, and she sprang up with him, so he turned aside until he halted at the far end of al-Hudaybiyah, at a spring of little water, from which people only took a little at a time. The people soon drained it, and they complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of thirst. He drew an arrow from his quiver and commanded them to place it in the spring. He said: "By Allah, it continued to gush forth water for them until they departed from it." The Quraysh were alarmed at his coming down upon them, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished to send to them a man from among his Companions. He called Umar ibn al-Khattab to send him, and he said: "O Messenger of Allah! There is no one in Makkah from the Banu Ka'b who would become angry for me if I am harmed, so send Uthman ibn Affan, for his clan is there, and he will convey what you intend." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Uthman ibn Affan and sent him to the Quraysh, saying: "Inform them that we have not come for fighting, but have come only as those making umrah, and invite them to Islam." He also commanded him to go to men in Makkah who were believers, and women who were believers, and enter upon them, and to give them good tidings of the conquest, and to inform them that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will make His religion manifest in Makkah, so that faith will no longer be hidden there.

Uthman set off and passed by the Quraysh at Baldah. They said: "Where are you heading?" He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has sent me to invite you to Allah and Islam, and to inform you that we have not come for fighting, but have come only as those making umrah." They said: "We have heard what you say; carry out your errand." Aban ibn Sa'id ibn al-As stood up to him, welcomed him, and saddled his horse. He mounted Uthman on the horse and gave him protection, and Aban rode behind him until he reached Makkah. The Muslims said, before Uthman returned: "Uthman has reached the House before us and circumambulated it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I do not think he has circumambulated the House while we are besieged!" They said: "What would prevent him, O Messenger of Allah, since he has reached it?" He said: "That is my assumption about him: that he will not circumambulate the Ka'bah until we circumambulate it together."

The Muslims and the polytheists mingled over the matter of the truce, and a man from one of the two sides shot a man from the other, and it became a battle. They exchanged arrows and stones, and both sides shouted, and each of the two sides took hostages from among them. It reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that Uthman had been killed. So he called for the pledge, and the Muslims rushed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was beneath the tree, and they pledged allegiance to him that they would not flee. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took hold of his own hand and said: "This is on behalf of Uthman."

When the pledge was complete, Uthman returned. The Muslims said: "Abu Abdullah, have you satisfied yourself with circumambulating the House?" He said: "Evil is what you thought of me! By He in whose hand is my soul, even if I had remained there for a year while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was staying at al-Hudaybiyah, I would not have circumambulated it until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) circumambulated it. The Quraysh invited me to circumambulate the House, but I refused!" The Muslims said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the most knowledgeable of us about Allah, and the best in his assumption!"

Umar had taken the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for the pledge beneath the tree, and all the Muslims pledged allegiance, except al-Jadd ibn Qays, while Ma'qil ibn Yasar was holding one of its branches, raising it above the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The first to pledge allegiance to him was Abu Sinan al-Asadi, and Salamah ibn al-Akwa' pledged allegiance to him three times: at the beginning of the people, in the middle, and at the end.

While they were in this state, Budayl ibn Warqa' al-Khuza'i came with a group from Khuza'ah, who were the trusted advisers (ayba nush) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the people of Tihamah, and said: "I left Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy and Amir ibn Lu'ayy, who have camped at the springs of al-Hudaybiyah, with them the milch camels with their young, and they will fight you and bar you from the House." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We have not come to fight anyone, but we have come as those making umrah. The Quraysh have been worn down by war and harmed by it. If they wish, I will grant them a truce, and they will leave me and the people alone. And if they wish to enter into what the people have entered into, they may do so. If they refuse except to fight, then by He in whose hand is my soul, I will fight them for this matter of mine until my neck is severed, or Allah will surely carry out His command."

Budayl said: "I will convey to them what you say." He set off until he came to the Quraysh and said: "I have come to you from this man, and I heard him say a statement. If you wish, I will present it to you." Their foolish ones said: "We have no need for you to tell us anything about him." Their men of judgment said: "Bring what you heard." He said: "I heard him say such and such." Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi said: "This man has offered you a course of right guidance, so accept it, and let me go to him." They said: "Go to him." So he came to him and began speaking with him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him something similar to what he had said to Budayl. Urwah then said: "O Muhammad! Consider: if you were to exterminate your own people, have you ever heard of any Arab who destroyed his own family before you? And if the outcome is otherwise, by Allah, I see faces, and I see a rabble of people who are likely to flee and leave you!" Abu Bakr said to him: "Suck the clitoris of al-Lat! Would we flee from him and leave him?" Urwah said: "Who is this?" They said: "Abu Bakr." He said: "As for you, by He in whose hand is my soul, were it not for a favor you once did me, which I have not repaid, I would have answered you!" He continued to speak with the Prophet (ﷺ), and whenever he spoke he took hold of his beard. Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah was standing over the head of the Prophet (ﷺ) with a sword, wearing a helmet. Whenever Urwah reached toward the beard of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he struck his hand with the sheath of the sword and said: "Keep your hand away from the beard of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)!" Urwah raised his head and said: "Who is this?" He said: "Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah." He said: "O treacherous one! Am I not striving to atone for your treachery?" Al-Mughirah had accompanied a group of people in the pre-Islamic period, killed them, and taken their wealth, and then came and embraced Islam. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "As for Islam, I accept it; as for the wealth, I have no share in it at all."

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 48, verse 10 (part 2 of 2):

Then ʿUrwa began to watch the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) closely. By Allah! Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) spat, his spittle fell into the palm of one of them, and he rubbed it over his skin and face. When he commanded them, they hastened to carry out his command. When he performed ablution, they nearly fought each other over his ablution water. When he spoke, they lowered their voices in his presence, and they did not fix their gaze on him out of reverence for him. ʿUrwa then returned to his companions and said: "O my people! I have been received as an envoy by kings: by Kisra, by Caesar, and by the Negus. By Allah, I have never seen a king whose companions revere him as the companions of Muhammad revere Muhammad. By Allah! If he spits, his spittle falls into the palm of one of them, who rubs it over his face and skin. When he commands them, they hasten to carry out his command. When he performs ablution, they nearly fight each other over his ablution water. When he speaks, they lower their voices in his presence, and they do not fix their gaze on him out of reverence for him. He has presented you with a sound proposal, so accept it." A man from the Banu Kinana said: "Let me go to him." They said: "Go to him." When he came within sight of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is so-and-so, and he is from a people who honour the sacrificial camels (budn, camels brought for sacrifice), so send them to him." So they sent the camels to him, and the people came out to meet him reciting the talbiya (the chant of "Here I am, O Allah, here I am"). When he saw this, he said: "Glory be to Allah! It is not right that these people should be barred from the House." He returned to his companions and said: "I saw that the camels had been garlanded and marked, and I do not think they should be barred from the House." Then Mikraz ibn Hafs stood up and said: "Let me go to him." They said: "Go to him." When he came within sight of them, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "This is Mikraz ibn Hafs, and he is a wicked man." He began to speak with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). While he was speaking with him, Suhayl ibn ʿAmr arrived. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Your affair has been made easy for you (p-٥٤٠٧)." Suhayl said: "Come, let us write a document between us and you." He called the scribe, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Write: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate." Suhayl said: "As for 'the Most Merciful' (al-Rahman), by Allah, we do not know what it is. Rather, write: 'In Your name, O Allah,' as you used to write." The Muslims said: "By Allah, we will not write it except as 'In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.'" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Write: 'In Your name, O Allah.'" Then he said: "Write: 'This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed to.'" Suhayl said: "By Allah! If we knew that you were the Messenger of Allah, we would not have barred you from the House, nor would we have fought you. Rather, write: 'Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah.'" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am the Messenger of Allah, even if you deny me! Write: 'Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah.'" Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On condition that you leave us free between us and the House, so that we may circumambulate it." Suhayl said: "By Allah! The Arabs must not say that we were pressed into this. But you may do so in the coming year." So he wrote it. Then Suhayl said: "On condition that no man of ours comes to you, even if he is upon your religion, except that you return him to us." The Muslims said: "Glory be to Allah! How can he be returned to the polytheists when he has come as a Muslim?!"

While they were in this state, Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl arrived, dragging his feet in his shackles, having come out from the lower part of Makka, until he threw himself among the Muslims. Suhayl said: "O Muhammad, this is the first person for whom I agreed with you that you should return him." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "We have not yet concluded the document." Suhayl said: "By Allah, then I will never make peace with you on any terms." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Then permit him for me." He said: "I will not permit him for you." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Yes, do so." He said: "I will not do so." Mikraz said: "We have permitted him for you." Abu Jandal said: "O assembly of Muslims! Am I to be returned to the polytheists when I have come as a Muslim? Do you not see what I have suffered?" He had been tortured severely for the sake of Allah.

ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab said: "By Allah! I had not doubted since I embraced Islam except on that day. I went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Are you not the Prophet of Allah?' He said: 'Yes!' I said: 'Are we not upon the truth, and our enemy upon falsehood?' He said: 'Yes!' I said: 'Then why do we accept humiliation in our religion, and return before Allah has judged between us and our enemies?' He said: 'I am the Messenger of Allah, and He is my helper, and I will not disobey Him.' I said: 'Did you not tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?' He said: 'Yes! Did I inform you that you would come to it this year?' I said: 'No!' He said: 'Then you will indeed come to it and circumambulate it!'" He said: "So I went to Abu Bakr and said to him what I had said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Abu Bakr answered me just as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had answered me, and he added: 'Hold fast to his stirrup until you die, for by Allah, he is indeed upon the truth.'" ʿUmar said: "Because of that, I did many deeds (of atonement)."

When he had finished with the matter of the document, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Arise, sacrifice, and then shave your heads." By Allah! None of them stood up, even when he said it three times. When none of them rose, he went in to Umm Salama and told her of what he had encountered from the people. Umm Salama said: "O Messenger of Allah! Do you want that? Go out, and do not speak a word to anyone until you have sacrificed your camel and called your barber, and he shaves your head for you." So he stood up and went out, and he did not speak to any of them until he had done that: he sacrificed his camel and called his barber, and he shaved his head. When the people saw this, they rose and sacrificed, and some of them began to shave the heads of others, until some of them nearly killed one another out of grief.

Then believing women came, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿O you who believe, when believing women come to you as emigrants﴾ [al-Mumtahana: 10], up to His words: ﴿the disbelieving women as wives﴾ [al-Mumtahana: 10]. On that day ʿUmar divorced two wives who had been his while they were polytheists. Muʿawiya married one of them, and Safwan ibn Umayya married the other. Then he returned to Madina, and on his way back Allah revealed to him: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory﴾ [al-Fath: 1], and the verses that follow. ʿUmar said: "Is it a victory, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes!" The Companions said: "Congratulations to you, O Messenger of Allah! But what about us?" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed about us: ﴿It is He who sent down tranquillity into the hearts of the believers﴾ [al-Fath: 4], the verse.

When he returned to Madina, Abu Basir, a man from Quraysh, came to him as a Muslim. They sent two men in pursuit of him and said: "The covenant which you made with us!" So he handed him over to the two men, and they set out with him until they reached Dhu al-Hulayfa. They stopped there and began to eat some dates they had. Abu Basir said to one of the two men: "By Allah, I see that your sword is excellent." The other drew it and said: "Yes! By Allah, it is excellent. I have tested it, and tested it again." Abu Basir said: "Show me, so that I may look at it." So he gave it to him, and he struck him until he was dead. The other fled running until he reached Madina, and he entered the mosque. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw him, he said: "This man has seen something frightening (zuʿran)." When he reached the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "By Allah! My companion has been killed, and I too am about to be killed." Abu Basir came and said: "O Prophet of Allah! Allah has fulfilled your covenant, for you returned me to them, and Allah has delivered me from them." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: (p-٥٤٠٩) "Woe to his mother! He would be a kindler of war, if he had anyone (to support him)." When he heard that, he understood that he would return him to them, so he went out until he reached the coast of the sea. Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl escaped from them and joined Abu Basir. No man of Quraysh who embraced Islam came out without joining Abu Basir, until a band of them gathered. By Allah! They did not hear of a caravan of Quraysh heading to Syria except that they intercepted it, killed its men, and took their property. Quraysh sent to the Prophet (ﷺ), appealing to him by Allah and by the ties of kinship, regarding what he had sent to them, and that whoever came to him would be safe. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you﴾ [al-Fath: 24], the verse.

The peace was concluded between the Muslims and the people of Makka on the terms of laying down war for ten years, that people would be safe from one another, that the Muslims would withdraw from them that year, and that in the coming year he would come and they would vacate the space between him and Makka, so that he could stay there three days. He would enter only with the weapons of a traveller, with swords in their sheaths. Whoever came to us from your companions, we would not return to you, and whoever came to you from our companions, you would return to us. Between us and you is a closed chest (ʿayba makfufa, a sealed container of trust), and there shall be no secret theft (islal) and no treachery (ighlal). They said: "O Messenger of Allah! Shall we give them this?" He said: "Whoever comes to them from us, may Allah keep him far away; and whoever comes to us from them, we will return him to them. Allah will grant him relief and a way out."

Beyond this, let the reader refer to the remainder of the benefits and subtleties of this expedition in (Zad al-Maʿad).

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[11] ﴿The bedouins who stayed behind will say to you, "Our wealth and our families kept us busy, so ask forgiveness for us." They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. Say, "Who could prevent Allah from you if He intended harm for you, or intended benefit for you?" Rather, Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do.﴾

﴿The bedouins who stayed behind will say to you, "Our wealth and our families kept us busy, so ask forgiveness for us"﴾ Mujahid said: They were the bedouins of Madinah, such as Juhaynah and Muzaynah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked them to accompany him on his departure to Makkah, but they said, "We will go with him to a people who have come against him and killed his companions, and we will fight them." So they made excuses with preoccupation. That is, they will say to you, when you rebuke them for staying behind from you: "Tending to our wealth and managing our livelihoods kept us from going out with you, and fear for our families of ruin. So ask forgiveness for us, our Lord."

As for His words, exalted is He, ﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts﴾, this is a denial of their excuse, and that what held them back is not what they claim; rather it is doubt in Allah and hypocrisy. Likewise their request for forgiveness is also not issued from reality, since it comes without repentance from them and without regret for what preceded of their disobedience in staying behind. In this there is a notice that the tongue carries no weight unless it expresses the true belief.

﴿Say, "Who could prevent Allah from you if He intended harm for you, or intended benefit for you?"﴾ That is: no one can prevent Him, exalted is He, from that, because no one overcomes Him. It is an indication that their asking forgiveness for them has no benefit while they remain upon their lying and hypocrisy. For this reason He threatened them with His words, glorified is He: ﴿Rather, Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do﴾, that is, He will recompense you for it.

A subtle point:

Al-Nasir said: The verse is not free of the device known to the scholars of rhetoric (al-bayan) as al-laff (the wrapping or interweaving of two elements within one expression). The original form, Allah knows best, would have been: "Who could prevent Allah from you if He intended harm for you, and who could withhold benefit from you if He intended benefit for you?" because this type of construction is typically used for harm. Likewise it occurs consistently in the Noble Book, such as His words: ﴿Who could prevent anything from Allah if He wished to destroy the Messiah, son of Maryam?﴾ (al-Ma'idah: 17) ﴿And whomever Allah intends to test, you will not control anything for him from Allah﴾ (al-Ma'idah: 41) ﴿So you could not avail me anything against Allah; He knows best what you spread therein﴾ (al-Ahqaf: 8). Among it is also his (ﷺ) saying in some hadith, addressing his clan: "I do not control anything for you," and similar examples are numerous.

The secret of its being specific to repelling harm is that the word "malik" (control) is in these contexts followed by the preposition lam, and repelling harm is a benefit that accrues to the one protected from it, whereas withholding benefit is not like that, since it is a harm that returns to the one deprived, not to him. When this becomes clear, the verse is structured in this way, because both parts share that each was negated to repel what is decreed of good and evil. When they were close, he combined them in one phrase, and he specified the phrase for repelling harm, because it is what is expected for these people, since the verse is in the context of threat or severe warning. It is comparable to His words: ﴿Say, "Who is it that can protect you from Allah if He intends for you evil or intends for you mercy?"﴾ (al-Ahzab: 17), for protection is only from evil, not from mercy. So these two verses are to be understood according to the principle I have mentioned, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 48, verse 12–13:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[12–13] ﴿Nay, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, ever. That was made attractive in your hearts, and you thought an evil thought, and you were a people ruined.﴾ ﴿And whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger, then indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a blaze.﴾ [al-Fath: 13].

﴿Nay, you thought that he would never return﴾, i.e., you believed that he would not come back: ﴿the Messenger and the believers to their families, ever﴾, i.e., nay, Quraysh would uproot them. ﴿That was made attractive in your hearts﴾, i.e., Satan beautified that for you and made it appear correct, until staying behind became beloved to you. ﴿And you thought an evil thought﴾, which is the non-support of the Messenger and the non-return of them from this journey of theirs. ﴿And you were a people ruined﴾, i.e., perishing, deserving the wrath of Allah, or corrupt in your deeds and your intentions. ﴿And whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger, then indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a blaze﴾ [al-Fath: 13], i.e., of the Fire, which blazes over them.

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[14] ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ Ibn Jarir said: This is from Allah, exalted is His praise, an exhortation to those Bedouin Arabs who stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to repent and return to the command of Allah by obeying His Messenger (ﷺ). He says to them: Hasten to repentance for your staying behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for Allah forgives those who repent, because He has always been One who pardons those who turn back to Him from their sins and disobediences against His servants, and One who is merciful to them by not punishing them for their sins after they have repented of them.

The discussion of the words of Allah the Exalted:

[15] ﴿The companions left behind will say, when you set out to take spoils, "Let us follow you." They want to change the words of Allah. Say, "You will not follow us; thus has Allah said before." Then they will say, "Rather, you envy us." Rather, they did not understand except a little.﴾

﴿The companions left behind will say﴾ — that is, with the excuse of being preoccupied with their wealth and families, after they had asked for forgiveness for themselves. ﴿When you set out﴾ — that is, when you intend to travel. ﴿To spoils﴾ — that is, their places. Ibn Jarir said: this refers to the spoils of Khaybar which Allah had promised the people of al-Hudaybiyah. ﴿Let us be⁠ — leave us⁠ — to set out toward them﴾ — that is, leave us to go with you. ﴿Let us follow you﴾ — that is, let us witness with you the fighting against its people. ﴿They want﴾ — that is, after their lies in the excuse and their request for forgiveness had become evident. ﴿To change the words of Allah﴾ — Ibn Jarir said: that is, the promise of Allah which He made to the people of al-Hudaybiyah. This is because Allah made the spoils of Khaybar theirs, and promised them that as a compensation for the spoils of the people of Makkah, since they had withdrawn from them under a treaty and had gained nothing from them.

Others said: rather, by His words, ﴿They want to change the words of Allah﴾, He meant their desire to go out with the Prophet ﷺ on a military campaign. Allah, blessed and exalted, has said in Surat al-Tawbah: ﴿So if Allah brings you back to a group of them and they ask your permission to go out, say, "You will never go out with me, and you will never fight an enemy with me."﴾ [al-Tawbah: 83]. Most scholars hold the first view. This is because the Prophet ﷺ returned from al-Hudaybiyah in Dhu al-Hijjah of the sixth year, remained in Madinah for the rest of it and the beginning of Muharram, then campaigned against Khaybar with those who had witnessed al-Hudaybiyah, conquered it, gained abundant wealth, and assigned it to them.

The commentators (al-shurrah) said: that happened by revelation. Then the expedition of Tabuk occurred after the conquest of Khaybar and also after the conquest of Makkah. And on his return from Tabuk the verse was revealed: ﴿They asked your permission to go out﴾ [al-Tawbah: 83], and so on. How, then, can it be interpreted as referring to what happened at the expedition of al-Hudaybiyah, when it was revealed long after it? — and Allah knows best. ﴿Say, "You will not follow us"﴾ — that is, to Khaybar, if we intend to march toward it. This is a negation with the meaning of a prohibition. Al-Shihab said: the statement is thus a figurative expression for the constructive prohibition, and it is more eloquent.

﴿Thus has Allah said before﴾ — Ibn Jarir said: that is, before our return to you: the spoils of Khaybar are for those who witnessed al-Hudaybiyah with us, and you were not among those who witnessed it; therefore you have no right to follow us to Khaybar, because its spoils belong to others. ﴿Then they will say, "Rather, you envy us"﴾ — that is, that we would obtain a share of the booty along with you if we were to join you; therefore you prevent us from going out with you. Al-Shihab said: this is a turning away from the claim that it is by the command of Allah; that is, rather, it is merely from your own selves, out of envy.

﴿Rather, they did not understand﴾ — that is, concerning Allah the Exalted, what is for them and against them in matters of religion ﴿except a little﴾ — that is, a little understanding, which was in worldly affairs, as in His saying, the Exalted: "They know an outward aspect of the worldly life."

The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted, saying:

[16] ﴿Say to the desert Arabs who stayed behind: "You will be called to face a people of great might; you will fight them, or they will submit. So if you obey, God will give you a good reward; but if you turn away as you turned away before, He will punish you with a painful punishment."﴾

﴿Say to the desert Arabs who stayed behind﴾, meaning: those who stayed behind from marching with you. ﴿You will be called to face a people of great might﴾, meaning: a might that exceeds the fighting of those I have fought, such that there is no room for peace or security in it. Rather, ﴿you will fight them, or they will submit﴾, meaning: they will enter into the religion without war or fighting. It was read irregularly (shādhdh) as "aw yusallimū" (أوْ يُسَلِّمُوا), with the meaning of "unless they submit" or "until they submit." ﴿So if you obey, God will give you a good reward﴾, meaning: the spoils in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter. ﴿But if you turn away as you turned away before﴾, meaning: from Hudaybiyyah. ﴿He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾, meaning: because your sin has doubled.

Then He specified from this threat those who have valid excuses, even if they arose after the first staying behind, with His, the Glorified, saying:

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[17] ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick, and whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger – He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow; and whoever turns away – He will punish him with a painful punishment.﴾

﴿There is no blame upon the blind﴾ Al-Mahayimi said: even if he is able to fight by perceiving the sound of the enemy's footsteps and the footsteps of his horse, yet it is difficult for him to protect himself from it. ﴿Nor upon the lame﴾, that is: even if he is able to fight while seated, yet he cannot advance and retreat (al-karr wa'l-farr), nor does he have the strength of one who stands. ﴿Nor upon the sick﴾, that is: even if he is able to see and to stand, he has no strength to repel the enemy, let alone overcome him.

Then God, exalted is He, indicated that these people, even if they miss out on jihad, their reward is not diminished if they obey Allah and His Messenger, by His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger – He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow; and whoever turns away﴾, that is, from obeying them both, even if he is blind, or lame, or sick: ﴿He will punish him with a painful punishment﴾, that is: with humiliation in this world, and the Fire in the next.

Note:

The exegetes differed concerning these people who are described as ﴿possessors of great might﴾, according to several opinions:

The first: they are the Hawazin.

The second: Thaqif, and the Prophet ﷺ campaigned against both of them.

The third: the Banu Hanifa, who followed Musaylima the Liar, and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) campaigned against them.

The fourth: the people of Persia and the Romans, whom 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) campaigned against.

The root of the disagreement is the general apparent meaning of the verse and the comprehensiveness of its application to all the mentioned campaigns. If the disbelievers of Makkah were counted among the possibilities, it would not be far-fetched; rather, in my view it is the closest, because the sin (in sa-) indicates near future, for this surah was revealed promising the conquest of Makkah on the Prophet's ﷺ return from al-Hudaybiyya, and following it was the Great Conquest campaign, in which none of the famous tribes stayed behind, since the Prophet ﷺ called them to fight the Quraysh or submit, so whatever happened of their Islam, whether willingly or unwillingly, came to pass – and Allah knows best.

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:**

[18] ﴿Allah was certainly pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree. He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquillity upon them and rewarded them with a near victory.﴾

﴿Allah was certainly pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree﴾ means the pledge of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at al-Hudaybiyya, when they pledged to him to engage Quraysh in battle, and not to flee, nor turn their backs to them, under a tree there.

The narrators in the (authentic) collections (al-Sihah) agree that the tree was not known afterwards. In the (two Sahihs) (al-Sahihayn, i.e., Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) it is narrated, from the hadith of Abu 'Awana, from Tariq, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: "My father was among those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) under the tree." He said: "We went out the following year on pilgrimage, but its place was hidden from us. And if it was made clear to you, then you know better." Also in both of them, from Sufyan, who said: "They differed regarding its location."

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) narrated from Qatada, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: "My grandfather, whose name was Hazn, was among those who pledged allegiance under the tree. We came to it the following year, and it was obscured from us."

Then Ibn Jarir said: "They claim that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, passed by that place after the tree had gone, and said: 'Where was it?' Some of them began to say: 'Here,' and some said: 'Here!' When their disagreement increased, he said: 'Move on. This is mere over-thinking.' The tree then disappeared; it was a samurah tree, either carried away by a torrent, or something else other than that." End of quotation.

(p-5417) al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in (Fath al-Bari): Ibn Sa'd narrated with a sound chain, from Nafi', that 'Umar was informed that some people were coming to the tree, praying beside it, so he threatened them, then ordered that it be cut down, and it was cut down!

This does not contradict what preceded, since it is possible that these people knew its place, or imagined it, and so took it as a mosque and a sacred place. 'Umar then cut it down, to protect their creed from shirk (associating partners with Allah), because gathering for worship around it would lead afterwards to worshipping it, just as the erecting of idols led to worshipping them. Its beginning was for magnifying what it represented and venerating the likeness of its people.

He also said in (Fath al-Bari), in explaining the words of Ibn 'Umar, "We returned the following year, and not two of us gathered at the tree under which we had pledged, which was a mercy from Allah," the following:

Al-Musayyib ibn Hazn, the father of Sa'id, agreed with what Ibn 'Umar said about the tree being hidden. The wisdom in that is that no temptation (fitnah) should result from it, given the good that took place beneath it. For had it remained, there would be no assurance against some ignorant people magnifying it, to the point that it might lead them to believe that it had some power to benefit or harm, as we see now, observed in what is less than it. Ibn 'Umar alluded to this with his words: "It was a mercy from Allah." That is: its concealment from them afterwards was a mercy from Allah, exalted is He. End of quotation.

This pledge is called the Pledge of Ridwan (Bay'at al-Ridwan), named after this verse, and its story has been mentioned previously in detail.

﴿So He knew what was in their hearts﴾, that is, of sincerity and resolve to fulfil the covenant. ﴿So He sent down tranquillity upon them﴾, that is, in patience, composure and dignity. ﴿And rewarded them with a near victory﴾. Ibn Jarir said: that is, He compensated them in the immediate term for what they had hoped to gain of the spoils of the people of Makkah through fighting them, with a near victory, and that, as it is said, was the conquest of Khaybar.

(p-5418)

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[19] ﴿And much booty that they will take. And Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise.﴾

﴿And much booty that they will take﴾ — this is the booty of Khaybar. It was land possessing date-palm orchards and wealth, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided it exclusively among the people of the Pledge of Ridwan. ﴿And Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise﴾ — that is, Mighty in His retribution against His enemies, and Wise in His governance of His creation.

The Discourse on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[20] ﴿Allah promised you much booty that you will take, and He hastened this for you and restrained the hands of the people from you, that it may be a sign for the believers and that He may guide you to a straight path.﴾

﴿Allah promised you much booty that you will take﴾ means what comes to them of the spoils of the disbelievers in the cause of jihad. ﴿And He hastened this for you﴾ means the spoils of Khaybar. As for the deferred spoils, they are all the conquests of the Muslims after that time, until the Hour arrives. It has been said: the hastened spoil is the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. The correct view is the first, as stated by Ibn Jarir (Ibn Jarir al-Tabari), because the Muslims did not gain any spoil after Hudaybiyyah, and they did not achieve a conquest closer to their pledge of allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Hudaybiyyah than the conquest of Khaybar and its spoils. ﴿And He restrained the hands of the people from you﴾ means the hands of the people of Khaybar, so that you prevailed over them, or the hands of the polytheists of Quraysh from you at Hudaybiyyah. Ibn Jarir chose the first, saying: because the second will be mentioned in His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you﴾ [al-Fath: 24], etc. That is, establishing a new meaning is better than emphasizing an existing one. But you may say: there is no barrier to emphasis, especially in a context of reminding of blessings and highlighting their significance. The second verse serves as an explanation of the first and a specification of its general sense, Allah knows best. ﴿And that it may be a sign for the believers﴾ means that this restraint or this spoil would be a lesson for the believers, by which they would know that they hold a position with Allah, Exalted is He, and that He guarantees their victory and conquest. ﴿And that He may guide you to a straight path﴾ means that He would increase you in insight, certainty and trust in the bounty of Allah.

And the words of Allah, Exalted is He:

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[21] ﴿And other [spoils] you were not able to obtain, but Allah has already encompassed them, and Allah is ever capable of all things.﴾

﴿And other [spoils] you were not able to obtain⁠﴾ is coordinated with "this," meaning: He will give you these spoils and other spoils, namely the spoils of Hawazin in the Battle of Hunayn, because He said: ﴿you were not able to obtain﴾, and this indicates that you had attempted them beforehand. Al-Hasan said: they are Persia (Fars) and the Byzantines (al-Rum). Al-Qurtubi said: their being hastened, although they were not realized except in the time of ʿUmar, is relative to the spoils of Islam that came after them.

From Qatada: they are Makkah. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: this statement of Qatada's is more consistent with what the apparent meaning of the revelation (al-tanzil) indicates. That is because Allah informed those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ under the tree that He encompasses a town they were not able to obtain. And it is understood that it is not said of a people, "they were not able to obtain this city," unless they had attempted it and it proved impossible for them. But when they had not attempted it, it cannot be said that they were unable to obtain it. Given that this is so, and given that it is known that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had not, before the revelation of this verse, targeted Khaybar for war, nor had he dispatched an army or a detachment to fight its people, it becomes clear that the meaning of His words ﴿and other [spoils] you were not able to obtain⁠﴾ is other than Khaybar, and that it is the one he had sought and attempted but failed to obtain. So Makkah and its people were of this kind. Allah, exalted is He, informed His Prophet and the believers that He had encompassed it and its people, and that He would grant them its conquest. End quote.

Al-Qurtubi said: the meaning of ﴿Allah has already encompassed them⁠﴾ is: He has prepared them for you. They are like a thing that has been encircled from all its sides, so it is confined and cannot escape. Thus, although you are not able to obtain them at present, they are held back for you and will not escape you. It was also said: ﴿Allah has encompassed them⁠﴾ means He knew that they would be yours, as He said: "and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge." It was also said: Allah preserved them for you, so that their conquest would be yours. End quote.

Regarding "other [spoils]," it is permissible that it be coordinated with "spoils" (maghanim), which is in the accusative governed by "He promised you," and that it be in the nominative as a subject (mubtada'), with ﴿you were not able to obtain⁠﴾ as its qualifier (sifa) and ﴿Allah has already encompassed them⁠﴾ as its predicate (khabar). There are other possibilities.

﴿And Allah is ever capable of all things⁠﴾ means: nothing is difficult for Him when He wills it.

Then, exalted is He, pointed to giving good news to the people of the Pledge of Ridwan (ahl bay'at al-Ridwan) of victory and continuous support, because of the sincerity of their faith, their sincerity in their steadfastness, and their preference for the good pleasure of Allah and His Messenger over every beloved thing, by His words:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[22–23] ﴿And if those who disbelieved had fought against you, they would have turned their backs; then they would not have found any protector or helper.﴾ ﴿[This is] the established way of Allah which has preceded [in the case of those who passed] before; and you will not find in the way of Allah any change.﴾ [Al-Fath: 23].

﴿And if those who disbelieved had fought against you﴾, i.e., after this conquest and the speedy victory. ﴿They would have turned their backs﴾, i.e., they would have turned their backs (ʾaʿjāz) to you in the battle, like the act of one defeated by his opponent in war. ﴿Then they would not have found any protector or helper﴾, i.e., anyone who would ally with them against your fighting and support them against you. ﴿[This is] the established way of Allah which has preceded [in the case of those who passed] before﴾ [Al-Fath: 23], i.e., it has taken place among the disbelieving communities of earlier nations along with their believers. ﴿And you will not find in the way of Allah any change﴾ [Al-Fath: 23], i.e., any alteration.

Ibn Jarir said: Rather, that is constant: for goodness there is its reward of goodness, and for evil and disbelief there is punishment and retribution.

(p-٥٤٢١)
