The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 48, verse 24:

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[24] ﴿It is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the heart of Makkah, after He had given you victory over them.* And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do.﴾

﴿It is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the heart of Makkah, after He had given you victory over them﴾: that is, He decreed between them and you the restraint and the withholding of hostilities, after He had granted you victory and dominance over them. This is an indication of the favour and blessing of the peace treaty at al-Hudaybiyyah, and that this was a care from Him, exalted is He, for what He preserved of their lives and their wealth, and His kindness to them on that day, for what He had stored up for them after it.

Some have held that by this restraint He meant what occurred on the day of the Conquest (fath), and they argued against this by saying that the surah was revealed before it.

Ibn Ishaq said: "Someone I do not suspect told me, from Ikrimah, the freedman of Ibn 'Abbas, that the Quraysh had sent forty or fifty men from among them, and ordered them to go around the army of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in order to seize some of his companions by surprise. So they were seized. He brought them to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he pardoned them and released their way." They had been pelting the army of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with stones and arrows. Ibn Ishaq said: "Concerning that, He said: ﴿It is He who restrained their hands from you﴾, to the end of the verse."

Ibn Jarir related from Mujahid, who said: "The Prophet of Allah ﷺ came forward performing 'umrah, and his companions seized some people from the people of the Sacred Precinct (haram) who were heedless, so the Prophet ﷺ released them." That is the "giving of victory" (idhfar) in the heart of Makkah.

Qatadah said: "The heart of Makkah is al-Hudaybiyyah."

﴿And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do﴾: that is, He will recompense you for it.

(p-5422)

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[25] ﴿They are the ones who disbelieved and barred you from the Sacred Mosque, and [barred] the offering detained from reaching its place of sacrifice. And were it not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, [and] that you might trample them, and thereby incur on their account a liability without knowledge — [that] Allah might admit into His mercy whom He wills. If they had been separated, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment.﴾

﴿They are the ones who disbelieved﴾: that is, these polytheists of Quraysh, they are the ones who denied the Oneness of Allah. ﴿And barred you from the Sacred Mosque and the offering﴾: that is, they also barred the offering, which is what is brought to Makkah of camels. ﴿Detained﴾: that is, held back. As-Samin said: It is said, "I detained the man from his need" when you held him back from it. Al-Farisi denied that (ʿakafa) takes a direct object, while Ibn Sida, al-Azhari and others affirmed it, and this is the apparent sense of the Qur'an, given the formation of the passive participle from it. End.

As for His words, may He be exalted, ﴿to reach its place of sacrifice﴾: Ibn Jarir said: that is, the place of its sacrifice. That is the entry into the Haram, and the place where, once it arrives, its sacrifice becomes permissible. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had driven with him, when he set out for Makkah on that journey, seventy camels.

In the verse there is evidence that the place of slaughtering the offering is the Haram.

﴿And were it not for believing men and believing women﴾: that is, present in Makkah among the disbelievers. ﴿You did not know them﴾: that is, by the attribute of faith while they were in Makkah; the polytheists there held them back from you, so they could not on that account come out to you. ﴿That you might trample them﴾: that is, that you might kill them along with the disbelievers, had you been permitted to conquer rather than make peace. As-Samin said: ﴿that you might trample them﴾ may be a substitute for "men and women," with the masculine given precedence, and it may be a substitute for the object of ﴿you did not know them﴾. So the estimate on the first is: "And were it not for the trampling of men and women who were not known." And the estimate on the second is: "You did not know their trampling," and the predicate is omitted, its estimate being: "And were it not for men and women being present, or in the vicinity." End.

﴿Then there would fall upon you from them a liability﴾: that is, sin and indemnity, from ʿarra, when something disagreeable befalls him. His words ﴿without knowledge﴾ are a circumstantial clause from the pronoun of the subject in ﴿you trample them﴾: that is, you would trample them while not knowing them.

Regarding the answer to "were it not (lawla)," there are opinions:

First: it is omitted, indicated by the sense of the discourse. The meaning: "And were it not for the aversion that you would destroy believing people among the polytheists while you do not recognize them, so that a disagreeable hardship would befall you by their destruction, He would have restrained your hands from them, and permitted you to enter Makkah to fight its combatants."

Second: it is mentioned, namely ﴿We would have punished﴾, and the answer to "if (law)" is the omitted one. So it is omitted from the first for the indication of the second, and from the second for the indication of the first.

Third: that His words ﴿We would have punished﴾ is the answer to both together, and this is remote if the literal sense of that is intended.

Al-Zamakhshari mentioned something close to this, for he said: It is permissible that "if they had been separated" be like a repetition of "and were it not for believing men," since both return to one meaning, and "We would have punished" is the answer. Al-Shaykh (Abu Hayyan) rejected both returning to one meaning, saying: because what the first is attached to is not what the second is attached to — conveyed by as-Samin.

An-Nasir answered with his words: Their reference here is only one, even though "lawla" indicates prevention due to existence, and "law" indicates prevention due to prevention. Between these two there is an evident contrast; because "lawla" here entered upon existence, and "law" entered upon His words "they had been separated," which refers to the non-existence of them. And the prevention of non-existence is existence. So both reduce to one matter from this aspect. He said: My grandfather, may Allah have mercy on him, used to prefer this second aspect, and he called it ṭarya (repetition for emphasis). It mostly occurs when the discourse is lengthy, and the time since its beginning has passed, and it is needed to return the latter to the former; sometimes he repeats it with the same wording, and sometimes with other wording that conveys its sense. Similar examples of both have already preceded.

Note: Ibn Ishaq interpreted "ma'arra" as blood money (diyya), on the view that the abode of war does not prevent that. This is the position of al-Shafi'i. Others held that it does prevent that, including Ibn Jarir, who said: "ma'arra" is the expiation for accidental killing, namely freeing a believing slave for one who is able to do so, and for one who is not able, fasting two months. He said: I chose this view over what Ibn Ishaq said because Allah only obligated on the killer of a believer in the abode of war — if he had not emigrated from it, and his killer did not know his faith — the expiation and not the blood money, saying: ﴿But if he is from a people hostile to you and he is a believer, then [the freeing of] a believing slave﴾ [an-Nisa 92], and did not obligate on his accidental killer his blood money. Therefore we say: by ma'arra in this place is meant the expiation. End.

﴿That Allah might admit into His mercy whom He wills﴾: this is connected to what the omitted answer indicates, as if it were said after it: "But He restrained them from you, and did not permit you to fight them, so that He might admit you into His complete mercy by preserving you from the liability." It is permissible that "whom He wills" is an expression for those among the polytheists who desired Islam; and Ibn Jarir restricted himself to this, saying: that is, that Allah might admit into Islam from the people of Makkah whom He wills, before you enter it. Abu al-Suʿud objected to this, that what follows it of the obligation of the revelation and the ordering of the punishment upon it refutes it.

﴿If they had been separated﴾: that is, if the polytheists of Makkah had been distinguished from the believing men and believing women whom you did not know among them: ﴿We would have punished those of them who disbelieved with a painful punishment﴾: that is, by killing, or capture, or another kind of delayed punishment.

Note: Al-Kiya al-Harrasi said: In the verse there is evidence that it is not permissible to burn the ship of the disbelievers if there are Muslim captives among them; likewise the shelling of fortresses when they are in them, and the disbelievers use them as a shield.

**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[26] ﴿When those who disbelieved had put zealotry into their hearts, the zealotry of ignorance, then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and made them adhere to the word of righteousness, and they were more deserving of it and worthy of it. And Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾

﴿When those who disbelieved had put zealotry into their hearts, the zealotry of ignorance﴾ Ibn Jarir said: That was when Suhayl ibn 'Amr put zealotry (al-hamiyyah) into his heart, so he refused to write in the treaty document that was drawn up between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the polytheists: "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful," and refused to write in it: "Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah." He and his people also refused to let the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) enter (Makkah) that year. The element governing the adverbial phrase (al-zarf) is either (la'adhdhabna) or (sadduukum), or (udhkur) implied, in which case it is the object (maf'ul bihi). Al-hamiyyah is al-anafah (disdain), namely arrogance and refusal. It is a verbal noun from (hamma min kadha) hamiyyatan.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers﴾ is a conjunction with an implied element (ma'tuf 'ala manwi). That is: the Muslims resolved to refuse that and to fight over it. ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers﴾ means the dignity and steadfastness, until they made peace with them on the condition that they return the following year, and on what had preceded.

﴿And made them adhere to the word of righteousness﴾ means He chose it for them, so the "obligation" (al-ilzam) is a metaphor for what was mentioned of choosing it for them, and He commanded them with it. ﴿And they were more deserving of it﴾ Abu al-Su'ud said: that is, they possessed a greater claim to it. Moreover, the form of comparison (sighat al-tafdil) indicates increase in general. It was also said: "more deserving of it" than the disbelievers. ﴿And worthy of it﴾ means those fit for it. ﴿And Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing﴾ Abu al-Su'ud said: that is, He knows the due right of everything, so He directs it to its deserving recipient.

(p-5426)

The commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 48, verse 27:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[27] ﴿Certainly did Allah fulfill for His Messenger the vision with truth. You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills, in security, with your heads shaved and your hair shortened, not fearing. But He knew what you did not know and has arranged before that a near conquest.﴾

﴿Certainly did Allah fulfill for His Messenger the vision with truth. You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills, in security, with your heads shaved and your hair shortened, not fearing.﴾ Ibn Jarir said: That is, Allah certainly fulfilled for His Messenger Muhammad his vision, which He showed him, that he and his companions would enter the Sacred House of Allah in security, not fearing the people of polytheism, some of them having shortened their hair and some of them having shaved it. Then it was related from Mujahid that he said: It was shown to him at al-Hudaybiyah that he would enter Makkah with his companions having shaved their heads. So when he slaughtered at al-Hudaybiyah, his companions said: Where is the vision of Muhammad (ﷺ)?

And from Ibn Zayd, he said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: "I have seen that you will enter the Sacred Mosque with your heads shaved and your hair shortened." But when he alighted at al-Hudaybiyah and did not enter that year, the hypocrites found fault in that and said: Where is his vision? So Allah said: ﴿Certainly did Allah fulfill for His Messenger﴾ to the end of the verse. "I did not show him that he would enter it this year, but it will certainly occur."

And: "the vision" (al-ru'ya) is in the accusative by the removal of the governing preposition, that is: He fulfilled it for him in his vision, meaning He made its truthfulness realized for him, as is the custom of the prophets, peace be upon them, and He did not make it into confused dreams (adghath ahlam). Or it is in the accusative as a second object, which is what al-Kirmani said; his wording is: (kadhaba, "to lie"), is transitive to two objects, one says: kadhabani al-hadith ("he made me a liar regarding the statement"), and likewise (sadaqa, "to tell the truth"), as in the verse. This is strange, because the doubled form (al-muthaqqal) is transitive to one object while the single form (al-mukhaffaf) takes two objects.

His saying: ﴿with truth﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) from "the vision"; that is, it is accompanied by truth, not among the confused dreams.

His saying: ﴿You will surely enter﴾ is the answer to an implied oath; that is: By Allah! You will surely enter.

His saying: ﴿if Allah wills﴾ makes the promise conditional upon the will of Allah, to teach the servants, or to indicate that some of them will not enter. So it means: those among you whom Allah wills to enter will surely enter it. Or it is a report of what the king of the vision said, or what the Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions.

His saying: "shaving their heads" is a circumstantial clause of anticipation (hal muqaddarah), because entering is in the state of ihram, not in the state of shaving and shortening. There is an elision in the statement, or it is an attribution of what belongs to a part to the whole. The meaning is: some of you shaving, and others shortening. The indication of this is that shaving and shortening cannot be combined, so each of them must be attributed to some of them.

It is established in the Sahih that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy upon those who shave!" They said: And those who shorten, O Messenger of Allah? He said: "May Allah have mercy upon those who shave!" They said: And those who shorten, O Messenger of Allah? He said: "May Allah have mercy upon those who shave!" They said: And those who shorten, O Messenger of Allah! He said: "And those who shorten!"

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿not fearing﴾ is an emphasizing circumstantial clause (hal mu'akkidah) to His saying "in security", or an establishing one (mu'assisah), because the active participle indicates the present state and the imperfect indicates the future, so it establishes for them security at the time of entering, and negates fear from them at the time of their settling in the city, not fearing anyone.

The Hafiz Ibn Kathir said: This occurred in the 'Umrat al-Qada' (the making up of the lesser pilgrimage), in Dhu al-Qa'dah of the seventh year, for when the Prophet (ﷺ) returned from al-Hudaybiyah in Dhu al-Qa'dah, he returned to Madinah, and he remained there in Dhu al-Hijjah and Muharram, and in Safar he went out to Khaybar, and Allah granted him its conquest, some of it by force and some of it by treaty. It is a great region, abundant in palm trees and crops, and the Jews there were employed upon it on a share basis. He divided it among the people of al-Hudaybiyah alone, and none witnessed it other than them, except those who came from Abyssinia: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and his companions, and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them all, and none of them was absent.

Ibn Zayd said: Except Abu Dujanah Simak ibn Kharashah, as is established in its place. Then he returned to Madinah, and when it was Dhu al-Qa'dah of the seventh year, he (ﷺ) went out to Makkah as a pilgrim of 'umrah, he and the people of al-Hudaybiyah. He assumed ihram from Dhu al-Hulayfah and drove with him the sacrificial animals. It was said there were sixty camels. He said the talbiyah and proceeded, and his companions were saying the talbiyah. Near Marr al-Zahran, he sent Muhammad ibn Maslamah ahead with horses and weapons. When the polytheists saw him, they were struck with a tremendous terror, and they thought that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was going to attack them, and that he had broken the covenant between them and him of ceasing fighting for ten years. So they went and informed the people of Makkah. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came and alighted at Marr al-Zahran, from where he could see the boundary markers of the Haram, he sent the weapons of bows, arrows and spears to the valley of Yajaj, and he proceeded with the swords into Makkah sheathed in their scabbards, as he had stipulated with them. When he was midway along the road, Quraysh sent Mikraz ibn Hafs, who said: O Muhammad! We did not know you to break the covenant! He (ﷺ) said: "And what is that?" He said: You entered upon us with weapons, bows and spears! He (ﷺ) said: "That did not happen, and we have sent them to Yajaj." He said: By this we knew you, by righteousness and fidelity. The heads of the disbelievers came out of Makkah, so that they would not look upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them, out of rage and fury. As for the rest of the people of Makkah, men, women and children, they sat on the roads and on the rooftops, looking at the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions. So he (peace and blessings be upon him) entered, with his companions before him saying the talbiyah, and the sacrificial animals had been sent ahead to Dhu Tuwa, while he was riding his she-camel al-Qaswa', which he had ridden on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, and 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah al-Ansari was holding the reins of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) she-camel, and he was saying:

Hemistich: In the name of the One other than whose religion there is no religion, in the name of the One whose messenger is Muhammad.

Hemistich: Clear the way, you sons of the disbelievers, from His path.

Hemistich: Today we will strike you for its interpretation.

Hemistich: As we struck you for its revelation.

Hemistich: A striking that removes the skull from its resting place.

Hemistich: And makes the close friend forget his close friend.

Hemistich: The Merciful has sent down in His revelation,

Hemistich: In scrolls recited upon His Messenger,

Hemistich: That the best killing is in His path.

Hemistich: O Lord! I believe in His word.

[p-5427] And Imam Ahmad related through the path of Abu al-Tufayl from Ibn 'Abbas that "when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) alighted at Marr al-Zahran in his 'umrah, it reached the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that Quraysh were saying: Do they not appear emaciated? His companions said: If we were to slaughter from our own backs, and eat from its meat, and drink from its broth, and in the morning we enter upon the people while we are strong. He (ﷺ) said: "Do not do that, but gather for me from your provisions." So they gathered for him, and spread out the leather mats, and they ate until they turned away, and each one of them filled his saddlebag. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came until he entered the mosque, and Quraysh sat toward al-Hijr. He (ﷺ) uncovered his shoulder with his cloak, then said: "Let the people not see any weakness in you." He touched the corner, then he entered until, when he was hidden by the Yemeni corner, he walked to the Black Corner. Quraysh said: Are they not content with walking? Indeed they are leaping like the leaping of gazelles! So he did that for three circuits, and it became a sunnah."

Abu al-Tufayl said: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, informed me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did that in the Farewell Pilgrimage. And Ahmad related through the path of Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions came to Makkah, and the fever of Yathrib had weakened them and they had suffered harm from it, the polytheists said: There will come upon you a people whom the fever of Yathrib has weakened and who have suffered evil from it. The polytheists sat on the side facing al-Hijr, so Allah the Exalted informed His Prophet (ﷺ) of what they had said, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded that they should perform ramal in the three circuits, so that the polytheists would see their strength. He said: So they performed ramal for three circuits, and he commanded them to walk between the two corners, where the polytheists could not see them. And in another narration: And the Prophet (ﷺ) was not prevented from commanding them to perform ramal in all the circuits except for sparing them."

[p-5430] In Ibn Kathir there are additional hadiths on this subject, so whoever wishes more may refer to them.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But He knew what you did not know﴾ means: of the good choice and the wisdom in turning you away from Makkah and preventing your entering it in that year.

Ibn Jarir said: That is His knowledge, He whose mention is exalted, of what was in Makkah of believing men and women whom the believers did not know. Had they entered it in that year, they would have trampled them with horses and on foot, and harm would have befallen them from them without knowledge, so Allah turned them back from Makkah on account of that. And so that He might admit into His mercy whom He wills of those He wishes to guide. ﴿and has arranged before that﴾ means: before your entering which you were promised in the vision of the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿a near conquest﴾, meaning the treaty which took place between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the polytheists of Quraysh, or the conquest of Khaybar, so that hearts of the believers might find rest in it until the promised conquest is made easy. Al-Zuhri went to the first view, he said: It means the treaty of al-Hudaybiyah. Nothing was conquered in Islam that was greater than it; fighting only happened where people met, but when the truce came, war was set down, and all the people became secure with one another, and they met and discussed matters and debated, and no one spoke with a person about Islam who understood anything without that person entering it. Indeed, in those two years there entered into Islam a number like those who had been in Islam before that and more. Mujahid agreed with him, and Ibn Zayd went to the second view.

Ibn Jarir said: The correct view is that it is general, so it is said: Allah arranged before that both of them.

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[28] ﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion, and sufficient is Allah as Witness.﴾

﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance﴾, i.e., with clear explanation; ﴿and the religion of truth﴾, i.e., Islam.

(p-5431) Al-Mahayimi said: "with guidance" means the decisive proofs; "the religion of truth" means the correct beliefs that conform most precisely to what is actually the case.

Ibn Kathir said: i.e., with beneficial knowledge and righteous action, for the sacred law (al-shari'ah) comprises two things: knowledge and action. Thus the legal knowledge is sound, and the legal action is accepted; its reports are true, and its commands are just. ﴿To make it prevail﴾, i.e., to make it high; ﴿over all religion﴾. Ibn Jarir said: i.e., to nullify by it all the creeds, so that no religion remains other than it. That will be when Jesus, son of Mary, descends, and kills the Dajjal (the Antichrist). Then all religions will be nullified except the religion of Allah with which He sent Muhammad (ﷺ), and Islam will prevail over all religions. End of quotation.

Ibn Taymiyyah said: Allah has made it prevail in knowledge, proof, and explanation over every religion, just as He made it prevail in power, victory, and support. The earth has been filled with it and with his community (ummah) in the eastern and western parts of the earth, and their dominion is lasting; no one can remove it, just as the kingdom of the Jews has ended, and the kingdom of those after them has ended from the best and central lands of the earth. End of quotation.

﴿And sufficient is Allah as Witness﴾, i.e., as a witness that what He promised of making His religion prevail over all religions, or of conquest, or of spoils, will certainly occur. Al-Hasan said: He bore witness for you concerning Himself that He would make your religion prevail over all religion.

Ibn Jarir said: This is an announcement from Allah, exalted is He, to His Prophet (ﷺ), and to those among his Companions who disliked the truce at Hudaybiyyah, that Allah will grant them victory over Makkah and other lands, consoling them thereby for the distress and grief they suffered when they turned back from Makkah before entering it and before circumambulating the House.

(p-5432) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[29] ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. And those with him are harsh against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and approval. Their mark is on their faces, the trace of prostration. That is their description in the Torah. And their description in the Gospel is like a seed which sends out its shoot and strengthens it, so it grows firm and stands on its stalk, pleasing the sowers – that He may enrage by them the disbelievers. Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds among them forgiveness and a great reward.﴾

﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him﴾ – i.e., his companions: ﴿are harsh against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves﴾ – i.e., they have severity and harshness toward the disbelievers who wage war against them and bar others from the way of Allah, and among themselves there is mutual compassion, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 54].

Subtleties:

The first: It is permissible regarding ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah﴾ that they be a subject and predicate, and that "the Messenger of Allah" be an attribute, or an appositive (ʿatf bayān), or a substitute (badal). ﴿And those with him﴾ is conjoined to it. Their predicate is: ﴿are harsh against the disbelievers﴾.

The second: Al-Shihab said: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿merciful among themselves﴾ is a complement (takmil). Had it not been mentioned, it might have been imagined that, due to their habituation to severity toward the disbelievers, that severity had become their disposition at all times and toward everyone. So when it was said: ﴿merciful among themselves﴾, that imagination was removed; it is thus a complement and a safeguard (ihtiras), as in the preceding verse, for when it was said: ﴿humble toward the believers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 54], it might have been imagined that the qualifying condition's implication is not considered and that they are described with humility always and toward everyone. So His saying: ﴿mighty against the disbelievers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 54] removed this. It is like the saying of the poet:

Forbearing when forbearance adorns its people, yet toward the enemy he is awe-inspiring.

(p-5433) The third: Al-Mahayimi said: The verse indicates that the religion of truth has manifested among his companions, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, since their irascible faculty has become balanced, following the balance of their thinking and appetitive faculties. For they are harsh against the disbelievers, due to their firm rootedness in sound belief, such that they are jealous on behalf of whoever's belief is not sound; ﴿merciful among themselves﴾ due to their not inclining toward desires. This is with regard to morals. As for regard to deeds, then: ﴿you see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and approval﴾. Ibn Kathir said: He described them with abundance of deeds and abundance of prayer, which is the best of deeds, and described them with sincerity therein to Allah, glorified and exalted, and seeking from Allah, exalted is He, abundant reward, which is Paradise, encompassing the bounty of Allah, glorified and exalted, which is the expansiveness of provision for them and His approval of them, exalted is He; and this is greater than the first, as He, majestic and exalted, said: ﴿And the approval of Allah is greater﴾ [al-Tawbah: 72]. End.

﴿Their mark is on their faces﴾ – a subject and predicate, i.e., their sign is present in them. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿the trace of prostration﴾ is an explanation of the mark, as if it were said: their mark, which is the trace of prostration; or it is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun within ﴿on their faces﴾.

Al-Shihab said: According to what precedes it, it is the predicate of a subject whose assumed form is: it is the trace of prostration. End. Do the faces (wujuh) signify the selves metaphorically, or literally? Regarding its meaning there are two interpretations from the early scholars. From Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿Their mark is on their faces﴾ means good bearing (al-samt al-hasan). Mujahid and others said: it means humility and lowliness. Mansur said to Mujahid: I did not think it was anything but this mark on the face. Mujahid said: Perhaps it is between the eyes of one who is harder of heart than Pharaoh.

Some of the early scholars said: "Whoever's night prayer is abundant, his face becomes beautiful by day." Ibn Majah traced it to the Prophet, but the sound view is that it is a statement of a companion (mawquf). Some said: Indeed, a good deed has light in the heart, (p-5434) radiance in the face, expansiveness in provision, and love in people's hearts. The Commander of the Faithful ʿUthman, may Allah be pleased with him, said: No one has concealed a secret except that Allah, exalted is He, has displayed it upon the surfaces of his face and the slips of his tongue.

Al-Tabarani narrated it as a marfuʿ report: "No one conceals a secret except that Allah, exalted is He, clothes him in its garment: if good, then good; if evil, then evil." Its chain is weak, because in it is al-ʿAzramī, who is abandoned (matruk).

Imam Ahmad narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "If one of you were to work upon a hard, solid rock that has no door and no window, his deed would come out to people, whatever it might be."

He also narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Indeed, good guidance, good bearing and moderation are a part of twenty-five parts of prophethood." Abu Dawud also narrated it.

The second interpretation of the verse is that these are traces seen on the face from the dust of the earth or the moisture of ablution. This was narrated from Ibn Jubayr and ʿIkrimah. And this was in the Prophetic era, when the mosque had no carpet except its dust and pebbles.

Each of the two meanings is from (sīmāhum) – may Allah be pleased with them and satisfy them.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That﴾ – i.e., the description: ﴿is their description in the Torah﴾ – i.e., their wondrous attribute therein: ﴿and their description in the Gospel is like a seed﴾ – i.e., its shoot: ﴿which sends out its shoot﴾ – i.e., its offshoots, or its ear, or its growth: ﴿and strengthens it﴾ – i.e., makes it strong: ﴿so it grows firm﴾ – i.e., the seed became thick and grew hard. The sin (in fastaghlaẓa) is for emphasis of thickness, or it passed from thinness to thickness: ﴿and stands on its stalk﴾ – i.e., stands straight on its stem. And (al-sūq) is the plural of sāq: ﴿pleasing the sowers﴾ – i.e., this seed which grew thick and stood on its stalk pleases those who sowed it, in its completeness, goodness of growth, and reaching its end. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿that He may enrage by them the disbelievers﴾ is a causal clause for what their comparison to the seed indicates of their growth and strength, as if it were said: He strengthened them and multiplied them only that He may enrage the disbelievers by them.

(p-5435) Subtleties:

The first: In His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and their description in the Gospel is like a seed﴾ there are two possibilities:

One: that it is a subject, and its predicate is ﴿like a seed﴾; so one stops at "in the Torah," and they are two parables. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas.

The second: that it is conjoined to the first "their description," so it is one parable in both books, and one stops then at "in the Gospel." This is the view of Mujahid and al-Farra'. In this case, His saying ﴿like a seed﴾ has several possibilities:

One: that it is the predicate of a implied subject, i.e., their description is like a seed, explained by the parable mentioned in the Gospel.

The second: that it is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun in "their description," i.e., resembling a seed whose description is this.

The third: that it is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, i.e., a parabling like a seed – mentioned by Abu al-Baqa'.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It may be that "that" is an ambiguous demonstrative clarified by His saying ﴿like a seed﴾, like His saying: ﴿And We decreed to him that matter, that the last of these would be cut off﴾ [al-Hijr: 66] – cited by al-Samin.

The second: Al-Samin said: The hidden pronoun in ﴿and strengthens it﴾ refers to the seed, and the visible one to the shoot. Al-Nasafi reversed this, making the hidden pronoun refer to the shoot and the visible one to the seed; i.e., the shoot was strengthened by the density of the seed, and its density is the abundance of its branches and leaves. Al-Jamal said: What al-Nasafi did is more fitting, for the custom is that the root is strengthened by its branches, which assist it and strengthen it.

The third: Al-Samin said: ﴿pleasing the sowers﴾ is a circumstantial clause, i.e., while it is pleasing. And here the parable is complete.

The fourth: Al-Zamakhshari said: This is a parable which Allah coined for the beginning of the affair of Islam and its progress in increase, until it became strong and established, because the Prophet ﷺ stood alone, then Allah strengthened him by those who believed with him, just as the first shoot of the seed is strengthened by what surrounds it of what sprouts from it, until it pleases the sowers. (p-5436) This is also what al-Baghawi said, that "the seed" is Muhammad, and "the shoot" is his companions and the believers; so he made the parable apply to the Prophet ﷺ and his community.

As for al-Qadi, he made it an example for the Companions only. His wording: It is a parable which Allah, exalted is He, coined for the Companions, who were few at the beginning of Islam, then they increased and became established, so their affair advanced to the point that it pleased people.

Al-Shihab said: Each has its direction.

The fifth: Ibn Kathir said: From this verse Imam Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, in one narration from him, derived the takfir (declaring disbelief) of the Rafidah who hate the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them. He said: Because they enrage them, and whoever enrages the Companions is a disbeliever by this verse. A group of scholars agreed with him in this. – End of Ibn Kathir's words.

It is not hidden from you that this is contrary to what the verifying scholars of Ahl al-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah have agreed upon: that none of the People of the Qibla is to be declared a disbeliever, as expounded in the book of creeds, and clarified by al-Nawawi in his commentary on the (Introduction of Muslim), and before him Imam al-Ghazali in his book (Fayṣal al-Tafriqa). Among the calamities of the middle centuries was the haste of jurists in declaring takfir and zandaqa. How much blood was shed in the cause of fanaticism for this, as many of them pass by the reader of history. Moreover, the consensus of the usulis is that the mujtahid, whatever he is, is rewarded and not blamed, not to mention the many differing opinions on their 'adalah, even in the smallest book of usul such as (Jam' al-Jawami'). Yes, extremism and excess in investigations is not the matter of the wise and fair. And when whiteness grows intense, it becomes leprosy.

﴿Allah has promised those who believe﴾ – i.e., who were truthful to Allah and His Messenger: ﴿and do righteous deeds among them forgiveness﴾ – i.e., pardon for what passed of their sins and bad deeds, by their good deeds; ﴿and a great reward﴾ – i.e., abundant reward, which is Paradise.
